title: Persist session archiving without restoring the session
body:
## The bug

Archiving a session in the Agents window could appear to succeed — the session vanished from the list — while recording nothing, so it reappeared after a refresh or restart. This hit hardest on old sessions whose working directories or worktrees no longer exist.

## Root cause

When a client dispatched `session/isArchivedChanged` for a session with no live host state, `AgentService.dispatchAction` first `await`ed `restoreSession(...)`. Restore reopens the session's working directory, and for a missing one **only an *already* archived session resumes read-only** — otherwise it tries to recreate the worktree and throws.

That is circular: archiving is precisely what would have made it archived. The operation was impossible for exactly the sessions that needed it most. The failed restore rejected the action, nothing was persisted, and the client never rolled back.

## The fix

Archived/read toggles are now applied **without materializing the session**: the flag is written to the session database and the catalogue delta is published via `root/sessionSummaryChanged`. The envelope and its side effects — worktree cleanup on archive, `onArchivedChanged`, Agent Merge sync — still run, since none of them need live state.

### Further bugs found and fixed along the way

- **`SessionSummaryNotifier` could not publish for an un-loaded session.** It re-derives summaries from live state and bails when there is none, so AHP-specified catalogue mutations were silently dropped. It now supports pushing changes into an announced summary, keeping a single notification path.
- **`removeSession` cleared the announced summary** — but it is also the idle-eviction hook, and eviction emits no `sessionRemoved`, so clients keep listing the session. A session that was opened and later evicted therefore looked *unknown*, and archiving it was dropped entirely. This is likely the most common archive flow (open a session, navigate away, archive later). The baseline now outlives eviction; `deleteSession` clears it explicitly.
- **The passive route was chosen from a stale snapshot.** `requiresSessionRestore` is computed at dispatch entry, but the callback runs behind earlier queued dispatches — so a toggle was dropped outright if an earlier action restored the session meanwhile. Residency is now re-checked at execution time, joining any in-flight restore.
- **The Agents window applied rejected envelopes.** It ignored `rejectionReason`, contradicting AHP reconciliation (a rejected action's optimistic effect must be reverted). It also flipped the archived observable with no connection to persist through.

## Protocol conformance

Dispatching a session action while *not subscribed* to that session is explicitly supported by AHP:

> "A client therefore answers by dispatching the ordinary `chat/*` action **to that chat's channel** — it does **not** need to have subscribed to the chat first." — `docs/specification/session-channel.md`

`dispatchAction` is a fire-and-forget notification, so the client is not owed an acknowledgement, and convergence for such clients is specified to ride `root/sessionSummaryChanged`, which is broadcast to every client regardless of subscription. Since that channel documents `read/done state` as part of its payload, the previous behaviour was a **conformance gap** — we dropped a mutation the protocol says we must publish. No protocol change was needed.

Creating `agentSessionData/<id>` is how Agent Host claims a session away from the extension host's Copilot CLI list, so the passive path refuses to do it for a session the host has never surfaced, matching AHP's "silently ignore actions for non-existent sessions".

## Out of scope

Un-adopted legacy Copilot CLI sessions (`ehcliAdoptable`) continue to be dropped rather than persisted, since persisting them would claim ownership away from the extension host. Filed separately.

## Testing

Nine regression tests added, **each verified to fail without the fix and pass with it**:

- persists + publishes without restoring (archive and read)
- succeeds when the working directory is gone (the motivating case)
- succeeds for a session that was opened and then idle-evicted
- lands when an earlier queued action restored the session
- creates no session database for an unknown session
- `deleteSession` still clears the announced baseline
- a rejected envelope leaves the session unarchived

Full suites green: 5,584 agentHost + 2,464 sessions + 1,222 workbench agentSessions. `typecheck-client`, `eslint`, and `valid-layers-check` all clean.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Float chat pills above the chat input
body:
## What

The sessions status pills sat inside the chat input part's layout, so the transcript ended where the pills began. This floats them above the input instead, so content renders and scrolls underneath.

The row lands in exactly the position it held in flow — verified in a headless browser against a replica of the production DOM: the row's rect is unchanged (`top 478, bottom 508, left 32, right 688`), the banner and composer don't move, and the list grows by exactly 34px (the 30px row plus the input part's 4px flex gap).

## How

New opt-in `IChatWidgetViewOptions.persistentContentHeight`. Setting it:

- floats whatever the host mounts into `ChatInputPart.persistentContentContainerElement`
- reserves the same space below the transcript via the list's existing `paddingBottom`
- keeps the scroll-to-bottom button, the input scrim and the suggest-next widget clear of the floating content

Only the Agents window sets it (`SESSION_CHAT_INPUT_TOOLBAR_HEIGHT`, the row's rendered height). Every other chat widget keeps the previous in-flow `display: contents` layout — the float and the space reservation are one switch, so a host can't get half of it.

The row itself is click-through so the transcript stays interactive behind it. Its pills take hit-testing back and now paint an opaque background: `chat.list.background` as the base, with the (translucent) secondary button color composited on top via `background-image` — the same technique `.chat-scroll-down` already uses. Verified a 10%-alpha pill over a red backdrop renders `rgb(53,53,53)`, fully opaque.

`ChatListWidget.scrollToEnd()` now scrolls through the new padding. `reveal` stops at the last item's edge, so without it the list would never report being at the bottom and both auto-scroll-while-streaming and the scroll-down button would break.

## Trade-offs

- Right-clicking the empty space beside the pills no longer opens the visibility menu; right-clicking a pill still does. The deliberate 12px `.empty` strip that existed for that purpose is removed, since a click-through row can't be hit.
- The pills row's scrollbar slider can't be dragged for the same reason. It still shows the scroll position, and wheeling over a pill scrolls the row.
- The reserved space is a static constant, so it's held even while the row is hidden.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` clean
- `SessionChatPills` and `ChatTurnPills` unit suites pass
- All 26 `SessionChatPills_*` component fixtures render without errors
- Opt-out path re-verified live on a plain chat widget: `display: contents`, `position: static`, `pointer-events: auto`, scroll-down at `7px` — identical to before

The sessions pills screenshot baselines shift and need refreshing from CI.

title: Process listing fails when a process exits during scanning
body:
Fixes #186500

## Problem

On Linux, opening the process explorer (or anything that calls `listProcesses`) can fail with **"Listing processes failed"** whenever a short-lived process happens to exit while the list is being built. The reported error is `cat: /proc/<pid>/stat: No such file or directory`.

## Root cause

When GNU `ps` is unavailable, we fall back to `vs/base/node/ps.sh`, which enumerates numeric entries under `/proc` and then reads each process's `stat`, `cmdline`, etc. A process can exit at any point between enumeration and those reads:

- the `ls -d [0-9]*` enumeration itself races with process exit (`ls: cannot access '<pid>': No such file or directory`),
- the per-pid reads race too (`cat: /proc/<pid>/stat: No such file or directory` from `awk` reading `stat`, or errors from the `cmdline` redirection).

Any of these writes to stderr. `listProcesses()` in `ps.ts` treats **any** stderr output as total failure and rejects, so one vanished process out of hundreds kills the entire listing for the user.

## Fix

Every access to a process's files in `ps.sh` can race against that process exiting, so this change suppresses errors from those accesses and handles the vanished process gracefully:

- `2>/dev/null` on the `/proc` enumeration and on each per-pid read,
- an emptiness guard on the resident-set-size value so a failed `stat` read reports `0.0` memory instead of injecting an empty operand into the shell arithmetic (which would itself print an error),
- a comment explaining why the suppression is correct here.

The rest of the pipeline is unchanged: processes that still exist produce exactly the same output as before.

## Testing

- New regression suite in `src/vs/base/test/node/ps.test.ts`: spawns short-lived background processes while repeatedly executing the real `ps.sh`, asserts stderr stays empty across multiple rounds, with a quiet-system baseline control first. It is gated to run only where `/proc` exists (skipped elsewhere).
- Reproduced the bug deterministically before the fix on a real Linux environment (WSL2): under churn, **10/10** measurement rounds produced race stderr (`ls: cannot access '<pid>'` / `cat: /proc/<pid>/stat` shapes), while the quiet-system baseline was clean - proving the failures are churn-induced.
- After the fix: repeated measurement rounds under sustained identical churn produced **zero stderr**, and a quiet-system output-equivalence check (original vs fixed script, excluding the checker's own transient processes) showed identical listings.
- `npm run transpile-client` passes; targeted ESLint on the changed test file is clean; unit run of `Process Utils` shows the existing regex tests passing and the new Linux-gated suite correctly *pending* on Windows.

## Potential risks

- Low: behavior changes are confined to the fallback shell script used on Linux when `ps` is missing, plus the new test. Output shape for live processes is unchanged (verified by the equivalence check), so parsing in `parsePsOutput` is unaffected.
- A process that exits mid-scan now appears with placeholder values (or is omitted by the enumeration filter) instead of failing the whole listing - that degraded-but-useful row is strictly better than the current total failure, and matches what `ps` itself does under the same conditions.
- Not verified on macOS (unchanged code path) or inside a packaged VS Code client; the Linux verification was done against the real script in a real `/proc` environment rather than through the full app UI.

title: agentHost: Discover remote Copilot sessions
Cancelling cells of a closed notebook throws instead of being ignored
body:
Fixes #187448

## Problem

Cell cancellation is sent from the renderer to the extension host, but by the time it arrives the notebook document can already be gone - the notebook was closed, or the extension host restarted while cancellation was in flight. The lookup then throws `NO notebook document for 'file:///...'` straight out of the RPC dispatcher (`$cancelCells` -> `getNotebookDocument`), which is a long-running top error-telemetry bucket and interrupts whatever else the extension host was doing.

## Root cause

`$cancelCells` uses the strict overload of `getNotebookDocument` and has no guard for a missing document, unlike the kernel-lookup right above it in the same method which already handles a disposed kernel gracefully.

## Fix

`$cancelCells` now looks the document up in relaxed mode and returns silently when it is gone - there is nothing left to cancel. The existing behavior for live notebooks is unchanged.

## Testing

New test in `extHostNotebookKernel.test.ts`: cancelling cells of an unknown notebook URI is ignored (no throw, no interrupt call), and cancelling cells of a live notebook still reaches the interrupt handler.

Before the fix, the new test fails with exactly the production error: `Error: NO notebook document for 'file:///path/to/gone.ipynb'`. After: passing. Full `NotebookKernel` suite: 19 passing. `npm run typecheck-client` clean, ESLint clean on both changed files.

## Potential risks

None known - the only behavior change is for documents that no longer exist, where the previous behavior was an unhandled throw.

title: Notebooks of a view type break when their serializer registers twice
body:
Fixes #174051

## Problem

After a crash or restart of the extension host, an extension that provides a notebook serializer (for example the `sql-book` provider from the issue) registers again, but the stale registration from the previous extension host is sometimes still present. Registration then throws `notebook provider for viewtype 'X' already exists` out of the RPC dispatcher, the serializer never becomes active, and every notebook of that view type fails to open until the window is reloaded. This has been one of the top error-telemetry buckets for years.

## Root cause

`NotebookService._registerProviderData` treats an existing entry for the same view type as a hard error. That is correct for two different extensions fighting over one view type, but wrong when the *same* registration arrives again after an extension host restart and the old disposable was not run in time.

## Fix

Registering now replaces the existing entry instead of throwing:

- the fresh serializer takes effect immediately, so notebooks of the view type keep working across extension host restarts
- when the replacement switches extensions, that is logged as a warning (`ILogService`), since it indicates two extensions claiming the same type
- disposing a stale registration no longer removes the fresh entry — a registration only removes itself while it is still the current one
- the replace logic lives in a small exported helper (`registerProviderData`) so it can be unit tested without instantiating the service (its constructor claims process-global extension points)

## Testing

New test in `notebookServiceImpl.test.ts`: re-registering replaces the entry, reports the replaced extension id, stale disposal does not remove the fresh registration, and disposing the current one cleans up.

Before the fix, the equivalent call sequence fails with exactly the production error: `Error: notebook provider for viewtype 'sql-book' already exists`. After: passing. Also ran the neighboring `NotebookProviderInfoStore` suite (passing), `npm run typecheck-client` (clean) and ESLint on the changed files (clean).

## Potential risks

- Extensions that relied on the throw to detect duplicate view types will no longer see an error; the last registration wins, which matches what users expect (the newly activated extension works).

title: Fix element picker with mobile emulation
body: ## Summary Fix element picking under Mobile Emulation while preserving the emulated mobile presentation and page input behavior. Fixes #332182 ## Root Cause Mobile Emulation converts mouse input into touch input. Before contact begins, this conversion suppresses the pointer movement events that the element picker uses for hover highlighting. Disabling Mobile Emulation is not a suitable workaround because it can change the responsive layout and the element being inspected. ## Implementation - temporarily stop mouse-to-touch conversion while element selection is active - keep touch capability, the emulated viewport, and `(pointer: coarse)` active - keep the regular cursor for accurate element selection - suppress mouse-origin hover events while Mobile Emulation is active so picker activation and shutdown do not change page event delivery - restore mouse-to-touch conversion when element selection stops - synchronize suppression when Mobile Emulation changes and for newly adopted frames ## Scope and Risk The behavior change is limited to the Integrated Browser's Mobile Emulation and element picker. Normal Mobile Emulation continues converting mouse input into touch input before selection starts and after it stops. Desktop input behavior remains unchanged. ## Testing - `npm run transpile-client` - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-browser/preload-browserView.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserView.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserViewEmulator.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserViewFrameInspector.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserViewInspector.ts` - `git diff --check` - manually verified: - hover highlighting and rectangle selection under Mobile Emulation - all 19 monitored page event counters remain unchanged through hover, drag release, picker shutdown, and subsequent mouse movement - Mobile Emulation without the picker delivers Pointer and Touch events while Mouse events remain suppressed - returning to Desktop emulation restores normal Pointer and Mouse event delivery - Desktop to Mobile and Mobile to Desktop transitions while the picker remains active ## Reproduction Before the Fix With Mobile Emulation enabled, the circular touch cursor moves, but the element highlight does not follow the pointer.

title: Fix unfolding folded regions on Android vscode.dev
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/292361

## Problem
On **vscode.dev in Android Chrome**, folding a region works, but tapping the same region to unfold does not. The reporter’s video shows the inline fold placeholder (`...`), not only the gutter chevron.

This is a high-impact editor-folding bug: once a region is collapsed on a phone, there is no reliable way to get that code back without a reload or a desktop client. I prioritized it because the folding *model* is fine — the failure is in touch input — so a small, targeted fix restores a basic editing action on the web.

## Root cause
Two cooperating input bugs on Android phones (`PointerEventHandler` is used when `isIOS || isAndroid` and pointer events exist):

1. **Inline `...` placeholder (primary, matches the issue video)**  
   Gesture is registered only on `linesContentDomNode`. A tap on `...` is handled as a Gesture `Tap`, which calls `preventDefault()` and originally dispatched with `leftButton: false`. `FoldingController.onEditorMouseDown` returned immediately unless the event had a left or middle button, so the unfold path never ran.

2. **Duplicate `mouseup` on the gutter**  
   `PointerEventHandler` skipped touch `pointerdown` but still handled touch `pointerup`. Android Chrome also fires a compatibility `mouseup`. After unfold, the same icon is still under the finger, so the second `mouseup` immediately re-folded the region.

Android tablets were also left on `TouchHandler`, which never forwarded taps to folding contributions at all.

## What changed
- **`pointerHandler.ts`**: emit mouse down/up from Gesture taps (`PointerEventHandler` and `TouchHandler`) so folding sees the tap; ignore touch `pointerup` as well as `pointerdown`; use the pointer+gesture path on all Android devices, not only phones (`isMobile`).
- **`folding.ts`**: accept Gesture-shaped taps (`leftButton: false`) on `CONTENT_TEXT` (the `...` placeholder) and `CONTENT_EMPTY` (when `unfoldOnClickAfterEndOfLine` is on); clear `mouseDownInfo` after a successful toggle so a duplicate `mouseup` cannot toggle again.
- **`folding.test.ts`**: regression tests for duplicate gutter `mouseup`, placeholder tap unfold, and empty-content tap unfold.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run eslint` on the three changed files
- [x] `npm run typecheck-client`
- [x] `npm run compile-client` and `npm run compile-web` (0 errors)
- [x] Chromium folding unit tests, including the new `#292361` cases (3 passing in `folding.test.ts`; existing folding suites still green)
- [x] Manual: vscode.dev / Android Chrome — open a file, fold via gutter, tap `...` to unfold; fold/unfold again and confirm it does not snap back
- [x] Manual: gutter fold/unfold still works on desktop mouse

title: Restore persisted platform root config on agent host startup
body:
## Problem

The Agents window UI showed `chat.agentSessions.showExternal` as **Last 30 Days** while the agent host logged `showExternalSessions: 'none'` and hid external sessions.

`persistRootConfig` writes the whole root value bag to `agent-host-config.json`, but `_loadPersistedRootConfig` only restored five schema groups — customization, sandbox, copilotCli, agentMerge and proxy. Every `platformRootSchema` key was dropped on load, and [`AgentHostStateManager`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts) seeds only `permissions` and `telemetryLevel`, so those keys were genuinely absent from root config until a window connected and re-pushed them.

The host reads several of them before that happens, so they silently fell back to schema defaults.

## Evidence

From an `ah-logs` bundle, the `initialize` response carrying the host's cold-start root snapshot:

| Path in root-state snapshot | Present? |
| --- | --- |
| `config.schema.properties.showExternalSessions` | yes |
| `config.values.showExternalSessions` | **no** |

…even though `agent-host-config.json` on disk did contain `"showExternalSessions"`. A second window's `initialize` 48s later *does* carry the value — only because the first window had already re-pushed it.

The resulting sequence:

```
11:44:01  root/configChanged … "showExternalSessions":"none"
11:45:03  listSessions hid 48 of 394 session(s) (showExternalSessions: 'none')
11:46:32  showExternalSessions changed 'none' -> 'recent'; queueing session list reconciliation
```

`_getExternalSessionsMode()` fell through to `?? AgentHostExternalSessionsMode.None`, so the first catalog pass and the initial external-session reconciliation both ran under `none`.

## Impact beyond the reported symptom

The same gap affected every other `platformRootSchema` key read before a client connects:

- `codexAgentEnabled` — read during provider registration in `agentHostMain.ts` / `agentHostServerMain.ts`, so Codex could fail to register on a cold start
- `migrateLegacyCopilotCliEnabled` — read early in `listSessions`
- `editTelemetryEnabled`
- hand-edited values in a remote `agent-host-config.json`, which operators expect to be authoritative

## Fix

Restore the platform-owned keys alongside the other schema groups, via `platformRootSchema.validateOrDefault` so malformed entries still fall back to defaults rather than being loaded verbatim.

Root `permissions` stays excluded: it mirrors the connected client's managed settings, so reviving a previous run's value could re-grant an allow rule that has since been revoked. It is left for the client to republish.

## Testing

title: sessions: hide external Recent sessions superseded by newer local ones
body:
Adjusts the `Recent` external-sessions mode so it stops surfacing external sessions the user has clearly moved on from.

## What changed

`Recent` still shows the 2 most recently updated external sessions from the last 7 days, but now hides any of them that **2 locally created sessions have started after its last update**.

Implemented in `_getRecentSessionKeys` via a single cutoff — the start time of the 2nd-newest local session. An external session is dropped when its `modifiedTime` predates that cutoff:

| Local sessions | 10am external | 4pm external |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none after 10am | shown | shown |
| one at 11am | shown | shown |
| 11am + 5pm | **hidden** | shown |
| 5pm + 5pm | **hidden** | **hidden** |

## Why the cutoff is snapshotted

Sending a first message is what materializes a local session, so a cutoff derived on every listing would rotate an external row out of the list while the user is looking at it. `_getRecentSupersedingCutoff` therefore snapshots the value on the first `Recent` listing and refreshes it only when the external-sessions mode changes.

The existing external-session reconciliation listener is untouched, so the top-2 selection still rotates when external sessions are discovered or updated.

- Three setting/banner strings now read "up to the 2 most recently updated…" instead of promising exactly 2.

title: File watcher silently stops working when watched folder is renamed
body:
Fixes #309241

## Problem

When you rename or move a folder that is being watched recursively from outside the workspace, the file watcher never tells anyone. On Windows and macOS the underlying watcher handle survives the rename, so no events arrive at all: no `onDidDelete` for the base folder, and every later change inside the renamed folder goes unnoticed. The same rename inside the workspace behaves correctly, which is exactly the inconsistency reported in #309241.

I reproduced this on current main against the real `ParcelWatcher` backend: after renaming the watched root, the watcher delivered zero events, fired no fail signal, and stayed silent even for new files created inside the renamed folder.

## Root cause

`ParcelWatcher` only reacts to a lost watch path when an explicit `DELETED` event for the root arrives (`filterEvents` → `rootDeleted`). A rename produces no such event, so the existing recovery machinery in `BaseWatcher` (suspend/resume) never kicks in, and clients are left watching a ghost.

## Fix

This change adds a small periodic existence check on the watched root to `startWatching()`. If the root disappears without any event having been received, we synthesize the root `DELETED` event and run it through the exact same pipeline as a real deletion (`handleParcelEvents` → fail → suspend/resume). That means:

- clients now get `onDidDelete` for the renamed base folder
- the watcher enters suspend and automatically resumes when the path comes back
- polling watchers are untouched; Linux is unaffected because inotify already reports the rename as real events (and the new check backs off once the watcher has failed)

The check itself is one `fs.access` per watcher every 5 seconds (~0.05 ms per call measured), in line with the existing suspended-request monitoring cadence.

## Testing

- Added a regression test to the existing parcel watcher suite: `renaming watched path emits watcher fail and delete event if correlated`
- Verified it **fails before** the fix (timeout waiting for events) and **passes after** it
- Full parcel suite: 29 passing before and after, only pre-existing flaky failures unchanged
- Broader unit suite: 52 failures before the change on this machine, 52 identical failures after (all unrelated `agentHost`/environment issues)
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes; ESLint clean on both changed files

## Potential risks

- macOS behavior is expected to mirror Windows (FSEvents also keeps handles alive across renames), but I could only verify Windows locally
- The synthetic delete can arrive up to ~5 s after the actual rename

title: agentHost: add a chat contribution model for cross-cutting behavior
body:
Introduces a registry-driven contribution model for the agent host so cross-cutting behavior lives in self-contained modules instead of branches inlined in `AgentSideEffects` and `AgentService`.

The goal is that a feature which touches several points in the turn lifecycle (contribute a command, add context on the way out, strip it from rendered history) can be written once, in one folder, rather than as separate branchy code in each place.

## Hooks

| Hook | Fires |
|---|---|
| `onTurnEnd` | every terminal outcome, discriminated by a `TurnEndReason` union |
| `contributeSend` | before a turn is sent; results concatenated in `order` |
| `onHydrateTurns` | whole restored turn list, as a pipeline |
| `onAction` | client dispatched actions |
| `onUserMessage` | a user message admitted on the direct path |

## Contributions

`queueDrain`, `persistedTurnUsage`, `sessionTitle`, `checkpointAndChangeset`, `markdownPlanRichLinks`, `markUnread`, `githubReferences`, `chatSurface`, `worktreeAnnouncement`, `artifactTools`.

Each lives in its own subfolder and is registered explicitly in `createAgentService` from one shared list, mirroring `IAgentHostChangesetOperationService`. Sequencing comes from an explicit `order`; registration order is only a tiebreak.

## Supporting work

- A per-contribution context with chat and session scoped mementos, evicted centrally when a chat or session is disposed. This replaces the pattern of each collaborator keeping its own URI keyed map with its own cleanup path, and let `clearQueuedMessageSenders` and both of its call sites be deleted.
- Several collaborators that `AgentSideEffects` constructed privately are now services owned by the composition root: the session title controller, telemetry reporter, turn tracker, and local command dispatcher.
- The bespoke host bridge that existed because these were not injectable is down from seven members to two: `hostLaunchKind` and `sendTurnMessage`.

## Behavior

Behavior preserving throughout. The existing `agentSideEffects` suite is unchanged and still passes, which is the proof for each extraction. Full agent host suite after merging `main`: 6069 passing, 70 pending, 0 failing (`main` alone is 6037 passing).

## Known gaps, recorded in `chatContributions/TODO.md`

- The queued admission path does not attach GitHub references from a user message, while the direct path does. This predates the PR; it closes when turn admission is unified.
- Direct and queued admission now duplicate local command interception, title seeding, agent lookup, and telemetry setup. That duplication was previously hidden behind a bridge method; making it visible is deliberate, and `onIncomingRequest` removes it.

## Not done yet

- `onIncomingRequest` to unify turn admission, retire `sendTurnMessage`, and fold in the local command registry.
- Migrating the side chat (`/btw`) feature onto `contributeSend` plus `onHydrateTurns`, which should delete its per harness wiring in the Copilot and Claude agents and give Codex support by deletion.

## Merge status

`origin/main` is merged in. Upstream had changed `AgentHostTurnTracker.turnStarted` to take the agent object plus a trailing client id, and moved the tracker to `createInstance`; both call sites this PR created were updated, and the queued path passes its own sender client id.

title: Fix Markdown token cache invalidation for typographer

## Summary

Changing the `markdown.preview.typographer` setting previously refreshed the preview, but could reuse Markdown tokens parsed under the old option. An unchanged document could therefore keep straight quotes, dashes, ellipses, and symbol substitutions until another action forced it to parse again.

This change includes `typographer` in the token cache key. A configuration change now reparses the document, while repeated renders of the same document instance and version continue to reuse cached tokens.

## Regression Coverage

The new tests establish the cache contract:

- The same document instance and version parses once, verified with a Markdown-It core-rule counter.
- Changing a document's version invalidates tokens and renders its updated content.
- Changing `markdown.preview.typographer` invalidates tokens and applies typographic substitutions.

The test engine accepts an isolated Markdown-It plugin contribution solely to make parsing observable in the cache-hit test; production contribution handling is unchanged, and the existing test path still uses empty contributions. The version test uses a mutable `ITextDocument` fake because `InMemoryDocument` deliberately keeps text and version immutable. This preserves document identity while exercising version invalidation directly.

2. Set `markdown.preview.typographer` to `false` and run **Markdown: Open Preview to the Side**.

title: sessions: defer managed Changes tab reconciliation until working-set restore settles
body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---
🤖 

## Summary

Defer the single-pane managed Changes/Files tab reconciliation while a session working-set restore is in progress, then let the existing restore-end reconciliation apply the latest accumulated intent against the settled editor group.

This prevents the managed-tab coordinator from replacing a stale Changes tab concurrently with `IEditorGroupsService.applyWorkingSet`, which can dispose and recreate the editor group underneath that replacement.

## User-visible symptom and log evidence

While switching rapidly among recent Agent Host sessions in the Agents Window, the renderer repeatedly logged a canceled editor open immediately followed by a disposed scoped instantiation service:

```text
2026-08-21 18:34:57.934 [error] Canceled: Canceled
    at ...setInput
    at ...doOpenEditor
    at ...replaceEditors
    at ..._reconcileForeignChangesEditors
    at ..._reconcileCore
    at ..._reconcile
2026-08-21 18:34:57.934 [error] InstantiationService has been disposed: Error: InstantiationService has been disposed
    at ..._throwIfDisposed
    at ...createInstance
    at ...doInstantiateEditorPane
    at ...doCreateEditorPane
    at ...doShowError
    at ...replaceEditors
    at ..._reconcileForeignChangesEditors
```

I found 10 occurrences of `InstantiationService has been disposed` across recent Insiders sessions on August 19-21, all with the same managed-tab reconciliation path.

The second error is a consequence of the first: once the editor open is canceled, the editor pane attempts to show an error placeholder, but the old editor group's scoped instantiation service has already been disposed by the concurrent working-set replacement.

## Root cause

A session switch currently drives two related asynchronous paths:

1. `BaseLayoutController` applies the incoming session's editor working set under `_withSessionLayoutRestore(...)`.
2. `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator` observes the active-session change and immediately queues an ambient managed-tab reconciliation.

The coordinator's `_reconcileForeignChangesEditors` can therefore call `group.replaceEditors(...)` for the incoming session's Changes tab while `applyWorkingSet(...)` is still replacing the outgoing editor group. The coordinator holds the group captured before the asynchronous operation settles, so its replacement can continue against a group whose scoped services have since been disposed.

The controller already exposes the intended synchronization boundary:

- `ctx.isRestoringSessionLayout` is true for the full asynchronous restore.
- `ctx.onDidEndSessionLayoutRestore` queues a reconciliation after the restore depth returns to zero.

The ambient session-change path was not respecting that boundary.

## Fix

`queueReconcile` still records the latest target, merges triggers for the same session, and advances the generation while restoration is active, but it does not start work against the transient editor group.

`_reconcile` also checks `isRestoringSessionLayout` before consuming `_pending`. This covers work that was queued immediately before a restore began but had not started yet.

When restoration settles, the existing `onDidEndSessionLayoutRestore` listener queues the final reconciliation. Because `_pending` was retained rather than discarded, trigger intent is preserved and merged with the restore-end trigger, while the newest generation continues to supersede stale queued work.

This is intentionally not an exception filter and does not suppress `Canceled` or disposed-service errors. It removes the ordering race that causes them.

## Regression coverage

The tests cover both sides of the scheduling boundary:

1. A restore is already active when a session switch requests reconciliation. The test verifies that `queueReconcile` retains the intent without scheduling replacement, then applies it after restore end.
2. A stale Changes replacement is queued first, and a gated restore starts before the sequencer callback runs. The test verifies that the `_reconcile` guard leaves the old tab untouched during restore and that the restore-end reconciliation performs exactly one replacement for the active session.

Together they verify that:

- no `replaceEditors` call occurs against a transient editor group;
- the pending target is retained across restoration;
- exactly one replacement occurs after restoration settles;
- the resulting Changes tab belongs to the active session.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- focused managed-tab session-switch tests: 8 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser/desktopSessionLayoutController.test.ts`
  - 141 passing
- pre-commit hygiene checks on all changed files
- `git diff --check`

## Reviewer context

@sandy081, this touches the generation/pending-intent logic introduced as part of the recent single-pane lifecycle stabilization work. The key behavior to review is that pending intents remain accumulated during restore and are consumed only by the already-existing restore-end reconciliation, rather than being dropped or run against the outgoing group.

title: agentHost: retire the optimistic turn start on the first backend action
body:
Fixes #332087

## Problem

`ChatStateSubscription` applies the client's own `chat/turnStarted` optimistically and holds it in `_pendingActions` until the backend echoes it back carrying the originating `clientSeq`. The agent host does not send that `clientSeq`, so the reconcile takes the non-origin branch and the pending start is never retired.

`_recomputeOptimistic()` rebuilds the optimistic state on every confirmed action by replaying the pending list over confirmed state:

```ts
let state = confirmed;
for (const pending of this._pendingActions) {
	state = chatReducer(state, pending.action as IProtocolChatAction, this._log);
}
```

Replaying a turn start resets `activeTurn` to a fresh empty turn, so `activeTurn.responseParts` reads as empty no matter how many deltas have already been folded into confirmed state. The UI reads the optimistic state, so `_observeTurn` resolves the turn by id but sees no parts, `autorunPerKeyedItem` never creates a per-part observer, and `_setupMarkdownPart` is never called. On completion the turn moves into `state.turns`, which a replayed turn start does not touch, and the whole reply appears in a single step.

Measured in a live window with the renderer instrumented, on a prompt producing about 2.4 KB of markdown and no tool calls: 17 `chat/delta` envelopes arrived between 8.0s and 19.4s and all 17 passed the channel filter, confirmed `activeTurn.responseParts.length` was 1 from 8.0s onward, and the optimistic rebase rewrote it to 0 on all 19 recomputes. The markdown observer was created at 19.4s and emitted all 2,432 characters at once.

`_promotePendingTurnStartIfTerminal` already exists because the echo can arrive without the `clientSeq`, but it fires only for `chat/turnComplete`, `chat/turnCancelled` and `chat/error`. That is why the text lands all at once at the end: the promotion happens, just not until the turn is over.

## Change

Promote the pending turn start on the first backend action naming the turn instead of only on a terminal one, and rename the method to match.

Once any backend action for a turn arrives, the server has that turn, so the optimistic start is redundant and holding it can only mask confirmed state. The body is otherwise unchanged: the start is still applied to confirmed state when the backend has not created the turn itself, so an action that arrives before any server-side `chat/turnStarted` still has a turn to land on.

Nothing changes on the origin branch, where the echo does carry the `clientSeq` and the pending action is spliced as before, and nothing changes for a chat action without a `turnId`.

## How to test

1. In a Claude agent-host session, send a prompt that produces a long reply and no tool calls, for example "without using any tools, write a numbered list from 1 to 20 with one sentence per line about database indexing".
2. Watch the response area while it runs.

The text appears incrementally as it is generated. On `main` the response area stays empty for the whole turn and the entire reply appears at once when the turn completes. Same prompt and build, before and after: 2 DOM updates becomes 13, the markdown observer is created at 7.8s instead of 19.4s, and the renderer emits 16 times across 12 seconds instead of once.

Unit coverage adds one test asserting that a `chat/responsePart` and `chat/delta` arriving while the optimistic turn start is still pending are visible in the subscription value. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.

title: Derive chat extension enablement from chat.disableAIFeatures
body:
chat.disableAIFeatures is registered with ConfigurationScope.WINDOW, so it is accepted in remote and workspace settings, but applying it persisted a global disable for the chat extension. That list is machine wide and shared by every window on the client, so a value set only in remote settings also disables chat in local windows, and a local window cannot recover on its own because the remote window re-applies the disable on every start.

Add EnablementState.DisabledByAIFeaturesSetting and compute it in _computeEnablementState alongside the other window-derived reasons, so the extension is disabled exactly where the setting resolves. Nothing is persisted, which makes the state follow whichever settings.json applies to the window. canChangeEnablement reports false while the setting owns the state, and a configuration listener fires onEnablementChanged so the extensions view and the extension host pick the change up.

ChatTeardownContribution no longer changes enablement. It keeps hiding the auxiliary bar and requesting the extension host restart.

Installs that already recorded the global disable would otherwise keep it forever, so the enablement service drops that entry on startup once the setting resolves to true.

title: Modern UI: Fix CSS specificity for tab action fading
body: ## Problem In Modern UI, the editor tab action fade can use the wrong color or gradient direction in some cases. This regression was introduced by #331476. ### Reproduction Configure tab actions to overlay the tab label and appear on the left: ```jsonc { "workbench.experimental.modernUI": true, "workbench.editor.tabActionLocation": "left", "workbench.editor.tabActionReserveSpace": false, "workbench.colorCustomizations": { "modernEditorTab.activeBackground": "#faa", "modernEditorTab.activeActionBackground": "#f00", "modernEditorTab.activeHoverBackground": "#ffa", "modernEditorTab.activeHoverActionBackground": "#ff0", "modernEditorTab.hoverBackground": "#afa", "modernEditorTab.hoverActionBackground": "#0f0", "tab.selectedBackground": "#aaf", "modernEditorTab.selectedActionBackground": "#00f" } } ``` Hover over or focus the editor tab actions. Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/issues/3677 

Follow-up to #331896, which deferred the provider catalog wait on restore so a session that resolves from its own metadata doesn't pay for warming the whole catalog (~48s on a large `~/.copilot`).

It now asserts the guarantee instead: a session the provider cannot describe yet does not restore until the migration completes.

title: fix: align restoreSession migration test with lazy-catalogue read ordering (build fix for vscode-engineering#3677)
body:
## Build failure

The `main` unit-test task fails deterministically on one assertion:

```
AgentService (node dispatcher) > restoreSession > waits for initial provider migration before restoring a session
AssertionError: metadataCallsBeforeMigration: 1 (actual) vs 0 (expected)
```

The downstream `Publish Log Files` / `Verify non-production criteria` failures only cascade from this task exiting non-zero (`.build/logs` never produced).

## Root cause

The test `waits for initial provider migration before restoring a session` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts`) asserts that `restoreSession` performs **zero** `getChatMetadata` calls before the provider catalogue migration completes. That encoded the original eager-await ordering added in #331721.

Since then, the restore path was optimized to be lazy about catalogue warming: `_doRestoreSession` / `_restoreSessionState` now probe per-session metadata **once** via `getChatMetadata` first, and only await the O(catalogue) initial-provider migration when that probe misses (so a session that resolves from its own per-session lookup never pays to warm the whole catalogue — potentially ~48s on a large `~/.copilot`). title: agentHost: keep the parent output after a background subagent settles
body:
Fixes #332073

## Problem

`ClaudeSdkPipeline._processMessages` derives the turn from the prompt queue head:

```ts
const parent = this._queue.peekParent();
const turnId = parent?.turnId;
```

A parent that spawns background subagents ends its own turn, so the queue drains and everything that follows arrives with `turnId === undefined`. `ClaudeSdkMessageRouter.handle` then drops it:

```ts
if (turnId === undefined) {
	return;
}
```

When the subagents settle and the parent resumes producing output, every one of those messages is discarded. The chat stops at whatever the parent said before spawning, and the early return is silent at every log level, so nothing is reported. The transcript keeps all of it, which is why restarting the agent host makes the full response appear.

## Change

Anchor a message that arrives with no active turn to the turn a background subagent was spawned in:

- `SubagentSpawn` records the turn that spawned it, first-writer-wins like its other fields.
- `task_started` writes that turn onto the registry as a resume anchor. It lives on the registry rather than the spawn so it outlives `removeSpawn`, which `task_notification` performs on completion, and completion is exactly when the parent resumes.
- `ClaudeSdkMessageRouter.handle` falls back to the anchor for a message with no turn, and drops the anchor once a message arrives for a different turn.

The anchor is written by the concrete `task_started` event for that spawn's own `tool_use_id`, so when several background spawns are alive the most recently started one wins deterministically. Nothing scans the spawn map for a turn.

Nothing changes while a turn is active, or when no background subagent has been spawned: the early return still applies, so an idle session drops stray messages exactly as before.

## How to test

1. In a Claude agent-host session, send a prompt that spawns background subagents, for example "use subagents to audit these two directories in parallel, read-only".
2. Watch the chat while it runs.

The parent's output keeps appearing as the subagents report back. On `main` the response stops at the line before the spawn and never resumes, and restarting the agent host is the only way to see the rest.

Unit coverage adds two tests: one that the resume anchor outlives the background spawn that set it, and one end to end that output the parent produces after the subagent's completion notification still reaches the chat.

## Note on #331872

That PR hooks the same early return for `system` / `task_notification` so a background subagent's chip completes. This is the general case: once a turn is resolved the mapper handles `task_notification` normally, so this supersedes it and I am happy to close #331872 if this lands.

- **Before:** `strictPluginOnlyCustomization: true` blocks standalone skills, agents, hooks, instructions, and MCP servers.

- plugin-provided customizations remain eligible.

title: agentHost: resolve Claude customizations for a chat that is not resident
body:
Fixes #332047

## Problem

`ClaudeAgent.getChatCustomizations` resolves the chat through its live runtime:

```ts
const sess = this._findChatByUri(chat);
if (!sess) {
	return [];
}
```

`_findChatByUri` maps the chat to its backing's `sdkSessionId` and looks that up in `_chatEntriesBySdkId`, which holds only live `ClaudeAgentSession` wrappers. Two ordinary states have a backing and no wrapper:

- `_releaseChat` disposes the live session on idle eviction and keeps the backing on purpose: "`_chatBackings` retains the backing across release so the chat resolves uniformly on the next cold resume-on-send".
- `materializeChat` re-attaches the backing for a session restored into a fresh process, and registers no wrapper.

In both, the read returns `[]`, so the session reports no project commands, no skills, no agents, no rules, not even the read-only built-ins, until its next message. `AgentHostSkillCompletionProvider` resolves `/` completions through this call, so the session's slash commands are gone; `AgentService._doRestoreSession` seeds state only when the resolved set is non-empty; and `AgentSideEffects._publishSessionCustomizations` skips its dispatch when the resolved set already matches state, so nothing republishes later either.

An empty list is not the intended pre-materialize behaviour. `ClaudeAgentSession.getSessionCustomizations` supports a session with no SDK Query and documents it: "Pre-materialize there is no Query, so the full disk set is shown". A non-resident chat simply never reaches it. `CopilotAgent.getChatCustomizations` resolves from `resolveAgentChatContext(context, chat).configurationResource` and handles the "Provisional (pre-send) or pre-resume" case explicitly, and `CodexAgent.getChatCustomizations` resolves through `_resolveConversationSession`. `ClaudeAgent` is the only provider keyed on a live runtime, and the only one that ignored its `context` argument.

## Change

Read through a throwaway runtime built from the chat's exact backing. `_createProvisionalChatSession` is split into `_buildProvisionalChatSession`, which only builds, and a wrapper that registers it and re-applies client contributions for the send path. The read uses the build step, which starts no SDK Query and recovers the working directories from the SDK transcript `cwd` or the persisted overlay.

That runtime is never registered and is disposed when the read returns, so the read mutates no provider state. A resident one would make `_ensureResolvedChatSession` take the chat for a provisional one on the next send and materialize it fresh, and `isResume: false` starts the SDK with `sessionId` rather than `resume`, so a chat that has a transcript would silently begin a new conversation. The second test locks that. It would also queue an active-client refresh onto the session sequencer that could only run once the read had finished.

A failure reports no customizations rather than throwing, so a chat whose working directory cannot be recovered degrades to today's behaviour. The live-runtime path is unchanged.

Not covered: the client-pushed plugin tier, which a chat with no resident runtime still omits. Adopting it means running the plugin sync on every read, and reads happen per completion keystroke.

## How to test

1. Open a Claude agent-host session in a workspace that has `.claude/commands/*.md`, and send a message.
2. Close the window and reopen it, so the session is restored into a fresh host process.
3. Select the restored session and type `/` without sending anything.

The project's commands and the built-in skills are offered. On `main`, only `/rename` is.

Verified end to end in a dev container on 1.1.3: before the change the restored session's completions returned 1 item, after it they return 18 (5 project commands plus 13 built-in skills).

Unit coverage adds two tests to `claudeAgent.test.ts`: one that the read returns the pre-materialize set for a chat released from memory, and one that the read leaves no resident runtime behind and that the following send still resumes the existing conversation.

cc: @amunger 
## Summary

- add `parentTurnId` for immediate parent/child joins
- add `parentToolCallId` — the `task` call that spawned the subagent, stable across resumed turns
- report non-overlapping direct prompt, cache, completion, and billed-AIU usage per turn
- preserve existing inclusive UI usage and credit totals

Root turn spawns `level-1`, which spawns nested `level-2`. Each row reports only what *it* consumed; any subtree total is `Σ direct` over the rows reachable via `parentTurnId`.

| `turnId` | `parentTurnId` | `directPromptTokenCount` (emitted) | inclusive (derived) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `turn-parent` | — | 10 | 60 = 10 + 20 + 30 |
| `level-1` | `turn-parent` | 20 | 50 = 20 + 30 |
| `level-2` | `level-1` | 30 | 30 |

Each lane is one `agentHost.turnCompleted` row; each bar is one `languageModelToolInvoked` row. Blue bars are the main agent's own tool calls, gray bars are a subagent's, orange bars are `task` calls that spawn the lane below. The parent is blocked for exactly the child's lifetime, and `task X` / `task Y` run in parallel — which is why `child.parentToolCallId == task.toolCallId` is needed to pair each child with the call that spawned it. `parentTurnId` walks the same tree for cost.

title: launch skill: fix Windows launches always starting signed out
body:
## What

Two fixes to the `launch` skill's Windows launcher (`.agents/skills/launch/scripts/launch.ps1`), plus a documentation correction.

1. **Seed the shared-data-dir.** The launcher now copies the source shared-data-dir into the run's throwaway `shared-data` dir instead of handing Code OSS an empty one.
2. **Fix the auth preflight.** `Test-SourceHasGitHubAuthenticationSecret` now probes the shared database in addition to `globalStorage`, so its "no stored GitHub session" warning is accurate on Windows.
3. **Correct `SKILL.md`**, which documented the macOS-only auth model and recommended a remedy that cannot fix this on Windows.

The earlier commit on this branch (`c0afc1d`) is the unrelated fnm Node discovery fix.

## Why

On Windows the GitHub session is stored at `StorageScope.APPLICATION_SHARED` rather than `APPLICATION` — see `useSharedStorage` and `CROSS_APP_SHARED_SECRET_KEYS` in `src/vs/platform/secrets/common/secrets.ts`. That splits the credential across two directories:

| Piece | Location |
|---|---|
| Encrypted GitHub session blob | `<shared-data-dir>/sharedStorage/state.vscdb` |
| DPAPI-wrapped key (`os_crypt.encrypted_key`) | `<user-data-dir>/Local State` |

The launcher already copied the profile (so it had the key) but passed `--shared-data-dir` pointing at a brand-new empty directory (so it never had the blob). Every Windows launch therefore started signed out.

The failure mode was self-concealing: signing in again wrote the session to the shared dir, which the *next* launch discarded. macOS and Linux are unaffected — `isWindows` is false there, so the same token lands inside the copied profile, which is why this flow has always worked on macOS.

## Notes for reviewers

- The empty `--shared-data-dir` is still required for multi-instance isolation (concurrent instances otherwise fight over one SQLite file). This change seeds it rather than removing it, so isolation is preserved.
- The source shared-data-dir resolves to `~/<product.sharedDataFolderName>`, mirroring `IEnvironmentService.appSharedDataHome`. Override with `CODE_OSS_DEV_AUTHED_SHARED_DATA_DIR`.
- `Test-DbHasGitHubAuthenticationSecret` is split out from the old function and now returns `$false` (not `$null`) for a missing database, so `$null` means only "the probe failed". One intentional behavior change: when *both* databases are absent, the launcher now warns rather than staying silent.
- Nothing outside `.agents/skills/launch/` is touched; no product code changes. Hygiene skips `.md` and `.ps1` per `build/filters.ts`, confirmed by the precommit hook reporting `Hygiene checked 0 files`.

## Verification

Run on Windows 11, PowerShell 5.1, against a real authenticated profile:

- Launcher logs `copying shared data: ... -> ...` and no longer emits the sign-in warning.
- App log goes from `Clearing authentication for resource: https://api.github.com` to `Authenticating for resource: https://api.github.com/repos`.
- The Agents window shows no sign-in UI, and a chat request completes against the real service (credits billed).

No re-authentication is needed — existing sign-ins carry over, since both halves of the credential now survive the copy.

title: sessions: stop picking the harness by which one has models
body:
The New Session composer in the Agents window replaced the user's harness with the first one usable without GitHub, which in practice meant the first one that had published models. Models arrive asynchronously, so a user who picked Copilot or Codex while Claude was the only harness with a catalog watched the pick snap back to Claude a moment later.

This drops that substitution. The stored preference wins, and the first harness in the list is the default when there is no preference.

## What changed

`_preferUsableSessionTypeWhenSignedOut` is gone, along with its call site and the stale TODO above it. The pick goes straight into `openNewSession`.

There is a second, smaller fix. `_recreateOnProviderChange` rebuilds the draft on every session-type change while an explicit pick is set, even when the pick and the draft already agree. That was invisible before because the recreate is what carried the snap-back, so it always looked like it had a reason. Now that the harness no longer changes, it is a pure teardown of an untouched draft. The no-pick branch already checks whether the answer moved; the pick branch now does too.

## What was left alone

`resolveAgentAuthRequirement` still reads `agent.models`. It does not choose a harness, it answers whether one can run, and removing the model count would leave `SessionTypeAuthRequirement.Unusable` produced by nothing.

Worth a separate look: the picker greys out an unavailable harness with "No models available", but `getSessionTypeAvailability` returns `Available` whenever the chat session contribution has not registered yet, which is exactly the startup window this bug lived in. So that explanation never appears for the case reported here. Deliberate (the comment says not to lock a harness prematurely) and out of scope, but it means a harness that genuinely cannot run still fails on first send rather than up front.

## Verification

Ran against a real Agents window via the launch skill, with Claude holding models and the composer defaulting to it.

- Picked Copilot, held for 20s past the model-arrival window. Stayed Copilot.
- Picked Codex, held for 20s. Stayed Codex.
- Opened a new session. It honored the stored Codex preference.

Before the change both picks reverted to Claude within a second or two.

Unit tests: 43 passing across `NewChatWidget`, `SessionTypePicker`, `SessionTypePickerActionItem`, the session type auth requirement suite, and the auth gate. The new recreate test was checked against a disabled guard and fails without the fix.

The behavior this PR asks for, first-in-list default and stored-preference-wins, is already asserted by existing public tests on `SessionTypePicker`, so no new coverage was added for the deletion itself.

## Build failure

The `Compile` task failed for all platforms with a single TypeScript error, cascading into every downstream test/publish/verify job:

```
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts(9986,41): error TS2554: Expected 6 arguments, but got 5.
```

## Root cause

The test `restores the snapshotted default chat title after the session is renamed` constructed the service by calling the `AgentService` constructor directly:

```ts
new AgentService(new NullLogService(), fileService, createSessionDataService(db), { _serviceBrand: undefined } as IProductService, createNoopGitService())
```

This positional call does not match the current `AgentService` constructor, which takes an `IAgentServiceCore` first argument followed by DI-injected services (`ILogService`, `IFileService`, `ISessionDataService`, `IAgentHostGitService`, `ITelemetryService`). The service is not meant to be instantiated positionally in tests; every other test in the file builds it through the `createTestAgentService` helper, which wires up an `InstantiationService` and calls `createAgentService`. This lone direct construction passed 5 loose arguments where the constructor now expects 6, producing TS2554.

## How the fix works

The single call site is switched to the same `createTestAgentService(logService, fileService, sessionDataService, productService, gitService)` helper used by all sibling tests in the suite. The helper accepts exactly these five arguments (the remaining parameters are optional) and internally constructs the service via dependency injection, so the argument arity and types now match and the test compiles. Behavior is preserved: the helper produces a fully wired `AgentService` equivalent to what the test intended.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back.**

Public culprit commit/PR: not confirmed from public history in this checkout.

Rationale: This is a single-line, test-only typecheck error with an obvious, low-risk fix-forward that matches the established pattern in the same file. A fix-forward lands faster and more safely than reverting a larger feature change, and the impact is contained to CI rather than shipped users.

title: nes: add optimized PatchBased02 prompt strategy
body:
## Summary

Adds `patchBased02Optimized`, an implementation-neutral prompting strategy for the optimized inline-suggestion treatment. It inherits everything from `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers` (current/recent-file line numbers, cross-file edits/imports, disabled next-cursor prediction) and additionally bakes in the client, latency, and completions-unification knobs this unified model was tuned for, so a single `promptingStrategy` value carries the whole treatment rather than relying on many separate client settings or experiment/deployment toggles.

This makes the treatment self-contained enough to ship purely as the prompt template of a `copilot-proxy` `/models` deployment: the proxy only specifies `promptStrategy: "patchBased02Optimized"` and the client derives everything else.

Analogous to the change for 2-in-1 models made in this PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321755

### Baked-in configuration

`patchBased02Optimized` spreads the shared `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers` config and adds:

| Setting | Baked value |
| --- | --- |
| `patchModelPredictionKind` | `currentLineCompleted` |
| `splitPatchOnDiff` | `true` |
| `patchFastYieldLineWithCursor` | `true` |
| `extraDebounceEndOfLine` | `0` |
| `nesMimicGhostTextBehavior` | `true` |
| `cacheDelay` | `200` |
| `rebasedCacheDelay` | `0` |
| `debounce` | `0` |
| `supportsUnifiedCompletions` | `true` |

### How it works

- These are exposed as optional `ModelConfiguration` fields (each with a `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR` entry), following the same pattern used to bake in `allowImportChanges` and `supportsNextCursorLinePrediction`.
- Every read site resolves via `modelConfig.<field> ?? experimentDefault`, so behavior is unchanged for any strategy that does not set a value.
- `selectedModelConfiguration()` returns the strategy-resolved config, so consumers outside `xtabProvider` observe the baked values:
  - **xtabProvider** (`patchModelPredictionKind`, `splitPatchOnDiff`, `patchFastYieldLineWithCursor`, `extraDebounceEndOfLine`) via the already-resolved model config.
  - **NextEditProvider** (`cacheDelay`, `rebasedCacheDelay`) and **UserInteractionMonitor** (`debounce`) inject `IInlineEditsModelService`.
  - **inline completion provider** (`nesMimicGhostTextBehavior`) via its existing model service.
- Adds a reusable `NullInlineEditsModelService` test double for the newly-injected dependency.

### Completions unification

`supportsUnifiedCompletions` bakes completions unification into the strategy, following the exact `supportsNextCursorLinePrediction` precedent where a baked capability overrides the deployment toggle at each read site. When the selected NES model's strategy sets it, the client runs as the single unified provider — one baked boolean replaces all three unification settings:

- **`inlineCompletionProvider.ts`**: `unification` resolves via `selectedModelConfiguration().supportsUnifiedCompletions ?? InlineEditsUnification` (replaces `github.copilot.chat.advanced.inlineEdits.unification`).
- **`jointInlineCompletionProvider.ts`**: the baked flag is observed reactively (via `onModelListUpdated`) and OR-ed into the effective `modelUnification`, which both suppresses the separate GitHub Copilot completions provider and pushes `github.copilot` into the provider `excludes` (replaces `inlineCompletionsUnificationModel` (ExP) and `excludedProviders: "completions,github.copilot"` (local)).

The baked value never replaces the existing experiment path for other models — it only short-circuits it when set, so unrelated deployments are unaffected.

### Intended deployment

```jsonc
{
  "modelConfiguration": {
    "modelName": "copilot-suggestions-lysithea-0024",
    "promptingStrategy": "patchBased02Optimized",
    "includeTagsInCurrentFile": false
  }
}
```

No `inlineCompletionsUnificationModel` / `unification` / `excludedProviders` toggles are required — the strategy carries them.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck --prefix extensions/copilot`
- focused Vitest coverage for `applyStrategyConfig`, `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR`, `pickSystemPrompt`, `NextEditProvider` caching/speculative, and `UserInteractionMonitor`
- `npm run precommit`

title: agentHost: fix Copilot chat fork leaking an in-flight turn
body:
Fixes a race in Copilot chat forking. `_forkSdkChat` computed the SDK
fork boundary from a locally-mirrored SQLite column that is only filled
in after the next turn's `user.message` event streams back from the
SDK. If a user forked a turn while the following turn was still
in-flight, that column read as empty. The code treated an empty read
as "there is no next turn" and omitted the fork boundary entirely,
which silently copied the whole session, including the in-flight
turn's skill invocation and partial work, into the fork.

- Adds `CopilotAgentSession.waitForTurnEventId`, backed by a
  `DeferredPromise` on each `CopilotTurn`, so a fork can wait for the
  in-flight turn's event ID instead of skipping the boundary.
- Makes `CopilotTurn` a `Disposable` and `_currentTurn` a
  `MutableDisposable<CopilotTurn>`, so the turn's SDK event ID promise
  is rejected automatically whenever the turn ends, is superseded, or
  the session is disposed. This guarantees `waitForTurnEventId` always
  settles, so it needs no timeout.
- Updates `_forkSdkChat` to detect an active next turn via
  `currentTurnId` and wait for its event ID before forking, failing
  the fork outright if that turn never produces one.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

title: fix: always reserve tab action column when tabs wrap into multiple rows
body:
Fixes #331483

## Problem

In a wrapping (multi-row) tab layout, a tab that becomes dirty grows by the action-column width when `workbench.editor.tabActionReserveSpace` is disabled. That width change can push the row's last tab onto a new row (or pull one back on save), so the whole editor jumps vertically every time a modification indicator appears or disappears.

## Fix

Make `workbench.editor.wrapTabs` imply `tab-actions-reserve-space`: when tabs can wrap into multiple rows, the action column is always reserved, so dirty/pin indicators never change tab width. Single-row layouts are unchanged, and the default configuration (`tabActionReserveSpace: true`) already behaved this way.

This is the same class of fix as #330754 (reserve the close-button column so it doesn't overlap the label), closing the remaining gap for the wrapping layout.

## Evidence

Playwright geometry probe, Modern UI, `wrapTabs: true`, 12 tabs in 3 rows, dirtying `alpha-module.ts`:

| Config | Before/after | `alpha-module.ts` width | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tabActionReserveSpace: false` (before fix) | clean → dirty | 135px → **155px** (+20, reflows full rows) | unstable |
| `tabActionReserveSpace: false` (with fix) | clean → dirty | 155px → 155px | stable at 3 |
| defaults (before & after) | clean → dirty | 155px → 155px | stable at 3 |

Behavioral note: wrapped tabs now always show the tab action (e.g. close button) instead of only on hover — identical to the existing `tabActionReserveSpace: true` default, so the reserved column never reads as a blank gap.

## Tests

- New unit test `wrapping tabs always reserve tab action space to prevent row reflow (#331483)` in `editor.test.ts` asserts the `tab-actions-reserve-space` class follows `wrapTabs` even when `tabActionReserveSpace` is configured off (both at create time and via `enforcePartOptions`).
- `editor.test.js` suite: 16/16 passing locally.

Update (review feedback): the same width instability existed for tabs with hidden close actions (`tabActionCloseVisibility: false`): a clean `close-action-off` tab stayed compact while its dirty dot reserved the column. Wrapped titles now also carry a `tabs-can-wrap` class so CSS reserves the indicator column for close-hidden tabs as well (verified live: 154px → 154px; previously 135px → 155px), with matching cases added to the tab geometry test.

title: Agent Merge: recover from a checks fragment the host refuses
body:
Agent Merge could hang indefinitely on a pull request whose `checks` fragment GitHub refuses, showing the user nothing at all. I hit this on a real session and traced it from the agent host logs.

## What happens

When an organization enforces SAML SSO and the signed-in token is not authorized for it, the checks GraphQL query is refused with **HTTP 200 and a `FORBIDDEN` entry in the body** (hence the odd `authorization:200` in the logs). `microsoft/vscode` is public, so `core`, `mergeability`, review threads and comments all load fine — only `checks` fails, because it reaches into GitHub Actions data that is org-protected even on a public repo.

Verified by introspection: `CheckRun.checkSuite` is `CheckSuite!` (**NON_NULL**), so a refusal on the Actions data behind `checkSuite { workflowRun { workflow { name } } }` null-propagates and destroys the entire check node — the whole fragment fails, not just that one informational field.

From there, five things compounded into a silent, unbounded loop:

1. `checksPending(undefined)` returns `true`, so a fragment that never loaded read as "checks still running" and held the **fast** poll cadence — a measured steady ~66s re-request of a permanently refused query, forever, with no backoff.
2. `_scheduleAfterFailure` treated `authorization` as "just reschedule": no failure counting, no backoff.
3. `checks` therefore never satisfied `isCompleteHeadFragment`, so the gate was permanently `indeterminate`.
4. `indeterminate` was the only gate outcome with neither an action nor a budget — `prompt` has repeat/total caps and `terminal` disables, but `indeterminate` just rescheduled the backstop unconditionally.
5. Only `kind === 'authentication'` raised an auth requirement, so an `authorization` refusal never prompted the user. Agent Merge looked enabled and did nothing.

The generic reason string made it hard to diagnose too: one `"Pull request state is incomplete or stale"` covered five different fragments and never said which one, or why.

## The fix

- **Gate the workflow-name subselection** and drop it for a repository whose host refuses it, keeping the checks themselves. `workflowName` is purely informational (one consumer: repair-agent context in `agentMergeTools.ts`). The decision is remembered per repository so later polls don't re-pay for a rejected request.
  - Only the **rollup** request is retried. `_fetchExpectedCheckSuites` reads the same protected Actions surface and Agent Merge always requests it (`checks: { required: true }`), so a refusal there would otherwise be misattributed — re-running the whole paginated query for nothing and disabling workflow names on a repo where they were never the problem. That request now degrades to absent-and-incomplete instead.
- **Raise an auth requirement for `authorization`** as well as `authentication`, naming the organization and calling out SSO when GitHub reports it — turning a silent hang into an actionable prompt.
- **Give `indeterminate` a budget**, measured over *continuously observed* time. Evaluation is suspended while a turn runs and stops entirely while the host sleeps, so a gap between observations restarts the window rather than counting toward it. Keyed on a stable `cause` (e.g. `checks:authorization`) rather than the volatile reason text, so an oscillating reason can't defeat it.
- **Name the fragment and its error** in the indeterminate reason. `FragmentState.error` already carried this; it was simply never read.
- **Back off persistent authorization failures**, and stop an errored checks fragment from holding the fast cadence — `_setError` preserves the previous value, so this covers both the never-loaded and the stale-value cases.

## Safety

Partial check data is still never accepted. `throwGraphQLErrors` continues to throw on any non-empty `errors` array, so blocked nodes (which arrive as `null` because of the NON_NULL propagation) can never reach `toCheck`. Silently dropping refused checks could let Agent Merge conclude required checks passed and merge unsafely — the existing behaviour fails closed, which is correct; what was missing was **visibility**, not permissiveness. `classifyAgentMergeRequiredChecks` ignores `expectedSuites` entirely, so degrading it does not affect any merge decision.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` clean.
- 68 tests pass across the affected suites, including new coverage for the refusal fallback (with the Agent-Merge-shaped `{ checks: { required: true } }` config), the expected-suites refusal, and the fragment-naming reasons.
- The rewritten budget state machine was verified directly against the compiled method: continuous observation fires at 30 minutes, a 120-minute unobserved gap does not, a changed cause restarts, and it still fires after a restart.

title: Enhance Activitybar layout and item separation
body:
The Activity Bar hid view containers behind the "Additional Views" overflow menu while there was still room to show them. This was most visible with the compact Activity Bar and with Modern UI enabled, where it could collapse down to a single icon in a window that comfortably fits all of them.

### Changes

- Size the overflow computation from the current item height instead of a hardcoded 52px, which did not track the compact Activity Bar (28px) or Modern UI (36px + 8px gap) sizes.
- Publish the Modern UI inter-item gap from TypeScript as `--activity-bar-action-gap` and consume it in `floatingPanels.css`, so the rendered spacing and the overflow computation share a single source of truth rather than restating the same value in both places.
- Reserve the measured height of the global Accounts/Manage icons rather than deriving it from the overflow action size, which over-reserved by one gap. `GlobalCompositeBar.size()` has no remaining callers and is removed.
- Give back the one leading-item gap that the per-item stride folds into every item, since the gap only renders *between* items — without it the last item still overflowed a gap early.
- Add regression coverage for the per-item stride, the published CSS variable, and the leading-gap compensation across all four size combinations.

### Validation

- 21 `ActivitybarPart` unit tests pass.
- `typecheck-client`, ESLint, and hygiene are clean.
- Verified in a Code OSS dev build across classic and Modern UI at both default and compact sizes, sweeping window heights from 190px to 440px: the number of icons shown matches the space actually available at every overflow boundary, and items never overlap the global icons.

title: Refactor agentic browser opening lifecycle
Add trace logging to the multi diff editor
body:
Adds a `MultiDiffEditorLogger` that traces the state transitions which are hard to reconstruct after the fact when investigating multi diff editor bugs, such as the view jumping while scrolling or files being expanded even though they were collapsed.

### What is logged

- **View/content state** (observed): view model + loading changes, collapsed state changes no matter who caused them, and content height changes — annotated with `(above scroll offset)` when the change happens above the current scroll position, which is exactly what makes the view jump.
- **Programmatic scrolling**: `reveal`, restored scroll state (including whether it actually landed), and scroll adjustments coming from an embedded diff editor.
- **View state save/restore**: including the persisted active diff item (and when it cannot be found), plus editor set/clear input in both the multi diff editor and the sessions Changes editor.
- **Navigation**: go to next/previous change and go to file, recording whether the item had to be expanded.
- **Virtualization**: editor template acquire/release.

Per-frame rendering is deliberately not traced. URIs are logged as basenames to keep lines readable.

### Cost when disabled

The observing autoruns are only created while the log level is trace, and are disposed again when it is lowered, so nothing is observed and no state is tracked in the default case.

### How to use

`Developer: Set Log Level...` > `Window` > `Trace`, then reproduce the bug and read the `[MultiDiffEditor]` lines in the window log.

Sample output:

```
[MultiDiffEditor] view model changed (hasViewModel: true, isLoading: false, preserveFocusOnLoad: false)
[MultiDiffEditor] view items updated (items: 1, restoredDocStates: 0)
[MultiDiffEditor] collapsed state changed (changed: [test.js=false])
[MultiDiffEditor] content height changed (changed: [test.js: 540 -> 78], totalHeight: 78, scrollTop: 0)
[MultiDiffEditor] no active diff item after loading, selecting first change (items: 1)
[MultiDiffEditor] go to file (file: test.js, index: 0, position: first, focusEditor: true, wasCollapsed: false)
[MultiDiffEditor] set view state (scrollTop: 0, scrollLeft: 0, docStates: 1, collapsed: 1, activeDiffItem: <none>, viewItems: 1)
[MultiDiffEditor] applied pending scroll state (requested: {"top":0,"left":0}, applied: {"top":0,"left":0}, landed: true)
```
